title: The idea behind Frequency Lock Encoding
transcript: So Frequency Lock Encoding is a very simple idea, but it's just that: what if we intentionally inject frequency impairments, so, subtle frequency shifts, as a way of encoding data? And this is really powerful because now we can actually have another signaling layer, but we're not using any extra airtime, because we're just modulating the already existing signal. We're not using any extra frequency bands. We're just jittering the waveform ever so slightly. And we're not using any additional hardware or antennas or things like that. We're just modifying within the pull-in range of whatever synchronizer. So we call this idea a subprotocol. So we have a protocol living on top of another protocol. And so we can imagine a lot of different topologies, but the one that we care about is we can have a transmitter. And they're transmitting via their primary protocol to a receiver, but they're also transmitting to a secondary receiver through this subprotocol.
